clue.text: Lions in location establishing most important position

parts.note: a group of lions is called a pride
of can stand for in, as a man of the city is one in it
a place is a location

explanation.surface: Big cats moving into a site and taking over the top spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for the position of greatest honour or prominence.

clue.text: Weak legislation that brought relief to paupers?

definitions.text: Weak legislation that brought relief to paupers?

parts.note: poor means weak or of low quality
a law is a piece of legislation

explanation.surface: A feeble statute once meant to help the destitute.
explanation.walkthrough: The Poor Law was the old English system of relief for the destitute; 'Weak legislation' builds the name, while the whole clue describes it, playing on the other sense of poor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Poor Laws were English statutes providing parish relief for the needy, from Tudor times to the twentieth century.

clue.text: Notions coming from outside associations

indicators.note: coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Thoughts that arrive from links with people beyond the group.
explanation.definitionFit: Notions and thoughts are synonyms for concepts held in the mind.

clue.text: Surprisingly, internet contains article to amuse

indicators.note: contains says one piece holds the other inside it
surprisingly suggests the word internet turns out in an unexpected arrangement

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: The web, to everyone's surprise, holds a piece written purely for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' rearranges INTERNET to ENTERTIN, and 'contains' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse someone is to divert or delight them, an infinitive matching the verb.

clue.text: Swindle doctor

definitions.meaning: a swindle is a sham or fraud, a noun sense
to doctor is to falsify or tamper with something

explanation.definitionFit: A fraud is a sham thing, and to falsify a document is to counterfeit it.

clue.text: Communist record includes number in uprising

indicators.note: includes says the record word holds the next piece within it

parts.note: a list is a written record

indicators.note: in a down clue uprising means the piece is read from the bottom up

parts.note: nine is a number

explanation.surface: A party member's file holds a figure about a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Communist' looks like part of the surface's subject but is the definition; in a down clue 'uprising' turns the number upwards before it goes inside the record.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Lenin's doctrine is a Bolshevik-style communist.

clue.text: Start to clap competent guy?

indicators.note: start to means only the first letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: able means competent

explanation.surface: Begin applauding a capable fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' looks like a man, matching 'competent guy'; it is a guy rope, a stay or wire, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy is a rope or wire bracing a mast or tent, which a strong wire rope can serve as.

clue.text: Erstwhile sheep on island turned into spiced meat

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: erstwhile means former, past
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A former flock animal on an isle ends up as cured deli meat.
explanation.definitionFit: It is smoked, seasoned beef, a deli staple in sandwiches.

clue.text: It may create a scene that is spooky

definitions.text: It may create a scene that is spooky

indicators.note: spooky suggests the words a scene are eerily disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Something that might stage an eerie spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of A SCENE are rearranged, signalled by 'spooky', while the whole clue describes a ghostly sitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering to contact spirits of the dead can make an eerie spectacle.

clue.text: Passed six deliveries deposited by army man

parts.note: in cricket an over is six balls bowled
TA is the Territorial Army
Ken is a man's name

explanation.surface: A cricket over handed in by a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end; TA, the Territorial Army, is the British volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A car that has been passed on the road has been overtaken by another, both past participles.

clue.text: Courageous support leading to victorious day

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
VE Day marked Victory in Europe in 1945

explanation.surface: Backing that leads up to a day of triumph takes nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: VE Day, 8 May 1945, celebrated the Allied victory in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Courageous and bold are synonyms describing someone unafraid.

clue.text: Only half of the decade brings glory

definitions.meaning: a lustrum, also spelt this way, is a period of five years
glory in the sense of splendour or brilliance

explanation.surface: Just five years of a ten-year span yields honour.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is a rare variant of lustrum, a five-year period, which is half of ten years.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-year period is half a decade, and brilliant shine or distinction gives renown.

clue.text: Spared the rod and suffered no loss

definitions.meaning: not given a beating, as in the proverb about sparing the rod
having never been defeated in competition

explanation.surface: A child never thrashed and a team never defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: Not having been struck, and having never lost a match.

clue.text: Hostilities observed from European capital

parts.note: wars are hostilities
saw means observed

explanation.surface: Conflicts witnessed from a city in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital city of Poland.

clue.text: Dependency of country lacking leader — priest imprisoned

indicators.note: imprisoned says one piece is shut inside another
lacking leader says the country's first letter is dropped

parts.note: France is a country
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel

explanation.surface: A headless nation keeps a cleric jailed and relies on others.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel, a crossword staple; the beheaded country keeps him inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Trust in or dependence on someone is a state of needing support.

clue.text: Go up a castle awkwardly after start of engagement

indicators.note: after says the anagram follows the first letter
start of means only the first letter of engagement is used
awkwardly suggests the words a castle are clumsily rearranged

explanation.surface: Climb a fortress clumsily once the battle has begun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' rearranges A CASTLE into SCALATE, placed after E from 'start of engagement'.
explanation.definitionFit: To intensify or rise in level is to climb higher, an intransitive verb sense.

clue.text: Notice manner of speech indicating junkie's problem

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
diction is a way of speaking

explanation.surface: A poster in a style of talk that reveals a drug user's trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Dependence on drugs is the habit that troubles a user.

clue.text: City that's turned insane with idiot strangling copper

indicators.note: turned says the word for insane is read backwards

parts.note: mad means insane

indicators.note: strangling says the idiot wraps round the copper

parts.note: an ass is a fool or idiot
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A deranged fool throttles a policeman in some town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' works on the insane word alone, and 'strangling' wraps the idiot round the metal's chemical symbol; 'that's' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital of Syria, an ancient urban centre.

clue.text: Chart showing a loan put in vehicle

indicators.note: put in says the following pieces go inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a lend is an informal word for a loan

explanation.surface: A diagram showing money lent being placed in an automobile.
explanation.walkthrough: Lend as a noun is informal British English, as in 'can I have a lend of it?'
explanation.definitionFit: A table of days and months is a chart of dates.

clue.text: Convincing bloke underpinning firm…

indicators.note: in a down clue underpinning means one piece sits below another

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a gent is a man, a bloke

explanation.surface: A fellow propping up a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A persuasive argument is clear and forceful.

clue.text: Diana hanging around with heather and not doing much

indicators.note: hanging around says the short form of Diana is turned back to front

parts.note: Di is short for Diana
ling is a kind of heather

explanation.surface: A woman lingers among moorland plants, being lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanging around' looks like loitering, a near-synonym of the definition, but it turns the short form of Diana back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Lazing about is the state of being inactive, a present participle.

clue.text: …he's a slippery customer portrayed as elegant?

parts.note: he refers back to the bloke of the previous clue, a gent
an eel is proverbially slippery

explanation.surface: Following on, the fellow is a shifty character pretending to be refined.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 18 down, so 'he' is the bloke there (GENT), and 'he's a slippery customer' adds EEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Refined and polite in manner is close to stylish, with the question mark showing affected gentility.

clue.text: Defender with gun pinning unruly characters in a raid

indicators.note: pinning says the gun holds the next piece fast inside it
unruly characters in says the letters of a raid run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: An armed protector holds down rowdy figures during an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defender' could suggest a footballer; 'unruly characters in' scrambles only the two words that follow, and the gun holds them.
explanation.definitionFit: A protector or keeper safeguards someone, as a defender does.

clue.text: Gloomy daughter needing nurture

parts.note: to rear a child is to nurture it

explanation.surface: A sad girl in need of care.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary and cheerless are synonyms for dismal.

clue.text: A hundred university chaps demonstrating perception

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
men are chaps

explanation.surface: A hundred college fellows showing insight.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen insight or shrewdness is sharpness of judgement.

clue.text: I wander northward to find new Zealand inhabitant

indicators.note: in a down clue northward means the whole run is read upwards

parts.note: to roam is to wander

explanation.surface: Roaming upcountry I meet a native of the islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northward' reverses the whole of I ROAM; the capital is moved in 'new Zealand' so that 'new' can't be read as a clue word, though the definition is New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: The indigenous Polynesian people of New Zealand are its first inhabitants.

clue.text: Nail one removed from woven material

indicators.note: removed from says one letter is taken out of the material

parts.note: braid is woven or plaited material
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A fastener taken out of some cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed from' takes I out of BRAID.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, small-headed tack is a type of nail.

clue.text: Mother-of-pearl necklace initially given unusual care

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of necklace
unusual says the letters of care appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: Jewellery handled with special attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'necklace initially' gives just one letter; 'given' is a link word, and 'unusual' scrambles only the word care.
explanation.definitionFit: The iridescent lining of shells is called nacre, the substance of pearls.

clue.text: Gosh, it's one hormone you can make synthetically!

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like gosh
'tis is an old contraction of it is
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation of wonder that a body chemical can be made in the lab.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation like 'Gosh!'; 'it's' gives the old contraction 'TIS. 'Synthetically' may look like an anagram signal, but the pieces need no rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A steroid produced by the adrenal glands, used as an anti-inflammatory drug, can be manufactured.

clue.text: Head of state's printed lie, as put about

indicators.note: put about suggests the letters are spun round and reorganised

explanation.surface: A leader's published falsehood is being spread around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put about' rearranges the letters of PRINTED LIE AS; 'put about' also hints at spreading a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to a president, as the adjective does, matches a possessive for the leader.
